_codes.GOOME_EDENIED: not allowed (permission or the user said no)
_codes.GOOME_EAGAIN: nothing yet, try again in a bit

_areas.core: These come from the shared code every backend goes through, so you can get them on any desktop. A lot of them have `<backend>` in front, thats whatever `goome_backend_name` says.
_areas.test: The test backend runs when `GOOME_TEST_*` is set or you ask for `GOOME_TEST`, and offscreen is `GOOME_MODE_OFFSCREEN`. See [Testing without a screen](testing.md) and [Offscreen mode](offscreen-mode.md).
_areas.x11: Linux on X11, or XWayland when goome falls back to it.
_areas.wayland: Linux on a Wayland compositor. What works depends a lot on the compositor, [Where it works](platforms.md) has the list.
_areas.gnome: Screen capture on GNOME (straight through mutter) and on KDE and the others (through the xdg-desktop-portal screen share popup). Both need glib and gstreamer at runtime. See [Screen capture](capture.md).
_areas.win32: Windows 10 and 11. Where theres an `(error <error>)` on the end its the `GetLastError` number, look it up in the Windows system error codes list if the text here isnt enough.
_areas.macos: macOS 14 and newer, through AppKit and ScreenCaptureKit.
_areas.loading:
Image loading messages come from `goome_bitmap_error()` (`Bitmap.LastError` in C#, and in the exception message in Python and Java). Theres no `goome` handle involved, so `goome_error` wont have them.

Fonts dont have messages at all. `goome_font_load`, `goome_font_load_mem` and `goome_font_system` give back `NULL` when the file cant be opened, is over 64 MB, isnt a font goome can read (.ttf, .otf and .ttc work), or for `goome_font_system` when fontconfig (`libfontconfig.so.1`) isnt there or has nothing that matches. Check the path first, then try the file in a font viewer.
_areas.ui: From the [UI kit](ui.md), these come out of `goome_error` after the frame where it happened.

goome.c|capture is off (no_capture) or t.what: `goome_capture` was called but either you set `no_capture` in the options or this desktop has no capture backend at all.
goome.c|capture is off (no_capture) or t.fix: Turn `no_capture` off if you set it. If thats not it, this session type just cant be grabbed, so use the test backend or a different session.

goome.c|no monitor <mon>.what: `goome_capture` got a monitor index that doesnt exist, either negative or past the number of monitors.
goome.c|no monitor <mon>.fix: Call `goome_monitors` and pass an index below the count it returns. Monitors can also come and go, so re-check after a display change.

goome.c|that rect is off monitor <mon>.what: The rect you gave `goome_capture` doesnt overlap the monitor at all once its clipped to the monitor area.
goome.c|that rect is off monitor <mon>.fix: Pass a rect inside the monitor `area`, or `NULL` to grab the whole monitor. Remember the rect is in that monitors own coordinates.

goome.c|no memory for the hit rects.what: `goome_end` couldnt allocate room to keep your click-through hit rects for the frame.
goome.c|no memory for the hit rects.fix: Nothing to do in the app except use fewer rects. If this really happens the machine is out of memory.

goome.c|<backend> cant take the keyboard.what: `goome_keyboard` was called on a backend that has no way to take keyboard focus, so `<backend>` is the name of the backend goome ended up on.
goome.c|<backend> cant take the keyboard.fix: Dont rely on keyboard input in that mode. Use `goome_hotkey` for global keys or switch to window mode, which can take the keyboard.

goome.c|<backend> cant grab the pointer.what: `goome_grab` was called on a backend that cant grab the pointer. `<backend>` is the backend name.
goome.c|<backend> cant grab the pointer.fix: Skip the grab on that backend or check the capabilities first. Window mode and overlay backends that support it are the ones that can do this.

goome.c|<backend> cant grab keys system.what: `goome_hotkey` was called on a backend with no system-wide key grab, which is common on Wayland. `<state_dir>` in the message is your control fifo path (or a hint to set `state_dir`).
goome.c|<backend> cant grab keys system.fix: Bind a key in your compositor or desktop settings that writes a line to that fifo, and set `state_dir` if goome says it has none. See [hotkeys](hotkeys.md).

goome.c|cant read the combo '<combo>'.what: `goome_hotkey` couldnt parse the combo string you gave it, so nothing was registered.
goome.c|cant read the combo '<combo>'.fix: Use modifiers and a key name joined with plus, like `ctrl+shift+k`. Check the spelling of the key name, see [hotkeys](hotkeys.md).

goome.c|only <n> hotkeys at once.what: `goome_hotkey` hit the limit of hotkeys goome keeps at once, `<n>` in the message.
goome.c|only <n> hotkeys at once.fix: Remove ones you dont need by calling `goome_hotkey` with a `NULL` combo and the same id, or reuse ids since the same id replaces the old combo.

goome.c|<backend> has no window to chang.what: One of the `goome_window_*` calls was made on a backend that has no real window, so there was nothing to change. `<backend>` is its name.
goome.c|<backend> has no window to chang.fix: Use window mode if you need to change the title, size or state. In overlay mode just skip the call.

goome.c|<backend> cant change the cursor.what: `goome_cursor` was called on a backend that cant change the pointer shape. goome still remembers the shape you asked for.
goome.c|<backend> cant change the cursor.fix: Ignore the error if you dont care, or draw your own cursor in the canvas. Window mode usually supports it.

goome.c|<backend> has no clipboard.what: `goome_clipboard_set` or `goome_clipboard_get` was called on a backend that has no clipboard.
goome.c|<backend> has no clipboard.fix: Dont depend on the clipboard there. Window mode or offscreen mode both have one, offscreen just keeps it in memory.

goome.c|the event queue is full.what: `goome_push` couldnt add your event because the queue of waiting events is already full.
goome.c|the event queue is full.fix: Poll events more often so the queue drains, or push fewer events per frame. The event wasnt added, so you can retry after polling.

goome.c|goome_resize is for offscreen mo.what: `goome_resize` was called while goome isnt in offscreen mode.
goome.c|goome_resize is for offscreen mo.fix: Only call it in offscreen mode. In window mode use `goome_window_size` instead.

goome.c|no memory for the clipboard.what: goome couldnt allocate a copy of the clipboard text, either while storing it with `goome_clipboard_set` or reading it back with `goome_clipboard_get`.
goome.c|no memory for the clipboard.fix: Nothing the app can do except copy less text. If it happens the machine is out of memory.

goome.c|no frame sent yet.what: `goome_frame`, or something that uses it like `goome_frame_copy`, was called before any frame was finished with `goome_end`, or the last canvas is no longer the current one for its monitor.
goome.c|no frame sent yet.fix: Draw and call `goome_end` at least once first, and then read the frame. If you resized or changed monitors, wait for the next frame.

goome.c|frame_copy: rect is off the <w>x.what: The rect you gave `goome_frame_copy` isnt fully inside the last frame, or its width or height is zero or negative.
goome.c|frame_copy: rect is off the <w>x.fix: Keep the rect inside the `<w>x<h>` frame size shown, or pass `NULL` to copy the whole frame.

goome.c|frame_copy: stride <stride> is t.what: The `dst_stride_bytes` you gave `goome_frame_copy` is smaller than one row of the copy needs, which is 4 bytes per pixel.
goome.c|frame_copy: stride <stride> is t.fix: Pass a stride of at least width times 4. Use the real row size of your destination buffer.

test.c|test backend: bad size <w>x<h>.what: The test backend was asked for a size under 1 or over 16384 in one direction, usually from `width` and `height` in the options or a `goome_window_size` call. Window mode also raises it to `min_width` and `min_height` first.
test.c|test backend: bad size <w>x<h>.fix: Pick a size between 1 and 16384. Check the size in your test script or options.

test.c|test backend: no memory for the c.what: The test backend couldnt allocate the canvas for the size you asked for.
test.c|test backend: no memory for the c.fix: Use a smaller size or scale. If the size is normal then the machine is out of memory.

test.c|test backend: cant read frames fr.what: The test backend was pointed at a frames source (`test_frames` or `GOOME_TEST_FRAMES`) but couldnt load the first frame from it. `<dir>` is that path.
test.c|test backend: cant read frames fr.fix: Check the path exists. Give a single `.ppm` file, or a folder with numbered files like `000000.ppm`, `000001.ppm` and so on, in a valid PPM format.

test.c|test backend: no memory for the f.what: The test backend ended up with no desktop frame to show, either because it couldnt allocate the fake one or the loaded frame was empty.
test.c|test backend: no memory for the f.fix: If you set a frames path, check that the file is a normal PPM. Otherwise the machine is out of memory.

test.c|test backend: nothing to grab the.what: `goome_capture` on the test backend got a rect that is empty once its cut down to the canvas, so there was nothing to copy.
test.c|test backend: nothing to grab the.fix: Use a rect that overlaps the test screen and has some width and height. Check your `test_frames` size and scale.

test.c|test backend: no memory for the g.what: The test backend couldnt allocate the buffer for a `goome_capture` result.
test.c|test backend: no memory for the g.fix: Grab a smaller rect. If it still fails the machine is out of memory.

test.c|test backend: no window in overla.what: A `goome_window_*` call was made on the test backend while it is in overlay mode, which has no window.
test.c|test backend: no window in overla.fix: Open goome in window mode for tests that use `goome_window_*`, or dont call those in overlay mode.

offscreen.c|offscreen: bad size <w>x<h>.what: `goome_open` in offscreen mode or `goome_resize` was given a width or height that is zero, negative or over 16384, or a scale outside 0 to 8. The scale in the message is `<scale>`.
offscreen.c|offscreen: bad size <w>x<h>.fix: Use a size from 1 to 16384 and a scale from 0 to 8. A scale of 0 means 1.

offscreen.c|offscreen: <w>x<h> px is too.what: Once the size is multiplied by the scale, the offscreen frame goes over 16384 pixels in one direction. `goome_open` or `goome_resize` returns it.
offscreen.c|offscreen: <w>x<h> px is too.fix: Lower the size or the scale so width times scale and height times scale stay at 16384 or less.

offscreen.c|offscreen: no memory for a <.what: goome couldnt allocate the pixel buffer for the offscreen frame size in the message.
offscreen.c|offscreen: no memory for a <.fix: Use a smaller size or scale. If the size is normal then the machine is out of memory.

offscreen.c|offscreen: no memory.what: `goome_open` in offscreen mode couldnt allocate its small state block.
offscreen.c|offscreen: no memory.fix: Nothing the app can do. The machine is out of memory.

offscreen.c|offscreen: no window, nothin.what: A `goome_window_*` call that offscreen mode doesnt handle was made, like `goome_window_drag`. Title, size, state and show do work offscreen, but there is no real window to move.
offscreen.c|offscreen: no window, nothin.fix: Skip dragging and moving calls in offscreen mode, or check `goome_mode` before calling them.

ui.c|ui style stack had <n> pushes left.what: A `goome_ui_push_*` call was never matched with a `goome_ui_pop` before `goome_ui_end`, so the frame ended with `<n>` styles still pushed. goome pops them for you and only reports this once.
ui.c|ui style stack had <n> pushes left.fix: Pair every push with a pop in the same frame, or call `goome_ui_pop` with the push count. Check early returns that skip the pop.

ui.c|ui pop of <n> but only <n> pushed.what: `goome_ui_pop` was asked to pop more styles than were pushed. The first `<n>` is what you asked for and the second is how many were there. goome only pops what exists and reports this once.
ui.c|ui pop of <n> but only <n> pushed.fix: Count your pushes and pops, they should match. A pop after an early return or a duplicate pop is the usual cause.

gnome.c|<method> failed: <reason>.what: A dbus call to mutter (`GetCurrentState`, `CreateSession`, `RecordMonitor`, `Start`) or to the portal came back with an error, and `<method>` is the call that failed. It comes out of `goome_open` or `goome_capture` while goome sets up the screen capture, and `<reason>` is whatever dbus said.
gnome.c|<method> failed: <reason>.fix: Read the `<reason>` text, its usually something like a service not running or access denied. Check that you are in a normal GNOME session with a session bus (`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` set) and that `xdg-desktop-portal` and `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` are running.

gnome.c|cant start gstreamer: <reason> (.what: GStreamer refused to build the capture pipeline that reads the screen stream from PipeWire. Nearly always the `pipewiresrc` element is missing, and `goome_open` or `goome_capture` gives this back.
gnome.c|cant start gstreamer: <reason> (.fix: Install `gstreamer1.0-pipewire` (plus `gstreamer1.0-plugins-base` for `videoconvert` and `videorate`). If its installed, the `<reason>` text says which element GStreamer couldnt find.

gnome.c|gstreamer wont play the stream f.what: The pipeline got built but GStreamer wouldnt switch it to playing for that screen, so goome has no frames from it. `<stream>` is the monitor connector name, or `screen 1` style when the portal is used.
gnome.c|gstreamer wont play the stream f.fix: Not sure what makes it refuse here, goome doesnt get a reason from GStreamer. Check that `pipewire` and `wireplumber` are running, then try again, or try the other capture backend.

gnome.c|mutter says no monitor is on.what: GNOME asked mutter for the monitor list and not one of them has a current mode, so every screen is off or unplugged. Comes from `goome_open` on the mutter backend.
gnome.c|mutter says no monitor is on.fix: Turn a display on (wake the screen or plug one in) and call `goome_open` again. If you are on a headless box there is nothing to capture.

gnome.c|the screen sharing portal never.what: Goome sent `<method>` to the screen sharing portal and no reply showed up before the timeout. 30 seconds for `CreateSession` and `SelectSources`, 5 minutes for `Start` since a person has to click the popup. It ends up in `goome_open` or later in `goome_capture` if the stream restarts.
gnome.c|the screen sharing portal never.fix: Look for a portal popup that is still open or hidden behind a window and answer it. If there isnt one, restart `xdg-desktop-portal` and `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` and try again.

gnome.c|screen sharing was turned down i.what: You (or whoever sat at the machine) clicked cancel on the GNOME screen sharing popup, so the portal said no. Comes out of `goome_open`, and `goome_capture` if the stream had to restart.
gnome.c|screen sharing was turned down i.fix: Call `goome_open` again and click Share this time. Goome keeps a restore token in its state dir so after the first yes the popup usually doesnt come back.

gnome.c|the screen sharing portal gave u.what: The portal answered `<method>` with a response that wasnt a yes and wasnt the user cancelling, and `<n>` is the response code (2 means it ended some other way). Comes from `goome_open` or `goome_capture`.
gnome.c|the screen sharing portal gave u.fix: Not sure what makes the portal do this, it doesnt say why. Check that `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` is installed and running, then retry. Deleting the saved `portal-token` file in goomes state dir is worth a try if it keeps happening.

gnome.c|no screencast portal, is xdg-des.what: Goome asked `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop` for its ScreenCast version and got nothing back, so there is no screencast portal on the session bus. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|no screencast portal, is xdg-des.fix: Install and start `xdg-desktop-portal` and `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome`, then log in again so the service is on your session bus.

gnome.c|the portal made no screencast se.what: The portal said yes to `CreateSession` but its reply had no session handle, so goome has nothing to attach the capture to. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|the portal made no screencast se.fix: Not sure why a portal would do that, it should always give a handle. Update `xdg-desktop-portal` and `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome`, restart them, and retry.

gnome.c|the portal shared no screens.what: The portal finished the share but the stream list was empty, so nothing was picked. That happens when the popup closes with no monitor selected. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|the portal shared no screens.fix: Open again and pick a screen in the popup before you hit Share. If the saved choice is stale, delete `portal-token` in goomes state dir so it asks fresh.

gnome.c|OpenPipeWireRemote failed: <reas.what: The portal wouldnt hand over a PipeWire connection for the screencast session, and `<reason>` is the dbus error. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|OpenPipeWireRemote failed: <reas.fix: Check that `pipewire` is running (`systemctl --user status pipewire`) and that `xdg-desktop-portal` is up to date. Then try again.

gnome.c|the portal gave no pipewire conn.what: The portal replied to `OpenPipeWireRemote` but no usable file descriptor came with it, so goome cant talk to PipeWire. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|the portal gave no pipewire conn.fix: Restart `pipewire` and `xdg-desktop-portal` and open again. Not sure what causes it beyond a broken portal install.

gnome.c|mutter never sent a pipewire str.what: Goome started the mutter screencast session and waited 5 seconds for it to announce a PipeWire node for every monitor, and at least one never did. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|mutter never sent a pipewire str.fix: Check that `pipewire` is running and not stuck, then retry. Switching to the portal backend is the other thing to try.

gnome.c|the screen streams are restartin.what: The monitors changed (plugged, unplugged, resolution) or a stream just died, so goome is rebuilding the capture and cant give a frame right now. `goome_capture` returns this and its temporary.
gnome.c|the screen streams are restartin.fix: Just call `goome_capture` again a moment later. Goome retries in the background, it usually takes under a second or a few.

gnome.c|no screen stream covers monitor.what: Goome has capture streams running but none of them overlaps the area of monitor `<mon>` (called `<name>`). Comes from `goome_capture`.
gnome.c|no screen stream covers monitor.fix: If you just changed your monitors, wait and call again. With the portal backend, make sure you picked that screen in the share popup, and delete `portal-token` in goomes state dir to be asked again.

gnome.c|no frame from <stream> yet.what: The stream for `<stream>` is running but hasnt delivered its first frame, after a wait of about 20 ms. `goome_capture` gives this back, most often right after `goome_open`.
gnome.c|no frame from <stream> yet.fix: Call `goome_capture` again. If it never goes away, the screen may not be changing (some compositors only send frames when something moves) or PipeWire is stuck.

gnome.c|that rect is too small to grab.what: The rect you passed to `goome_capture` ends up with no pixels once its mapped onto the monitor stream and clipped to the screen edges. That means a zero size rect or one fully off the monitor.
gnome.c|that rect is too small to grab.fix: Pass a rect that is at least a pixel wide and tall and sits inside the monitor area.

gnome.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> grab.what: Goome couldnt allocate the buffer for a `<w>`x`<h>` capture. This comes from `goome_capture` and means the machine is really out of memory or the rect is huge.
gnome.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> grab.fix: Grab a smaller rect or free up memory. Theres nothing else the app can do.

gnome.c|cant find libgio-2.0.so.0 / libg.what: Goome loads glib and gio at runtime for the dbus calls and couldnt find them, so GNOME capture is off. Comes from `goome_open` or `goome_capture`.
gnome.c|cant find libgio-2.0.so.0 / libg.fix: Install glib (`libglib2.0-0` on Debian and Ubuntu). Its on nearly every desktop already, so a container or minimal install is the usual reason.

gnome.c|cant find gstreamer, install lib.what: Goome loads GStreamer at runtime to read the screen stream and the libraries arent there. Comes from `goome_open` on the mutter or portal backend.
gnome.c|cant find gstreamer, install lib.fix: Install `libgstreamer1.0-0` and `libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-0`, plus `gstreamer1.0-pipewire` so the stream itself can be read.

gnome.c|<name> is missing from glib or g.what: A glib or GStreamer library loaded fine but is missing the function `<name>` that goome needs, which means the version is too old or odd. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|<name> is missing from glib or g.fix: Update glib and GStreamer to a current release from your distro. If you are on a custom build, check its the full library and not a stripped one.

gnome.c|cant reach the session bus: <rea.what: Goome couldnt connect to the dbus session bus, and `<reason>` is what glib said. Comes from `goome_open`.
gnome.c|cant reach the session bus: <rea.fix: Run the app inside your desktop session, not over plain ssh or from a service. If you need to, set `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` to the ones from your session.

macos.c|cant load appkit / libobjc: <rea.what: One of the system frameworks (libobjc, Foundation, CoreGraphics or AppKit) wouldnt load, and `<reason>` is what `dlerror` said. Comes from `goome_open`.
macos.c|cant load appkit / libobjc: <rea.fix: Run goome as a normal macOS app on a logged in desktop, not from a stripped sandbox or a headless ssh job. If `<reason>` points at a missing file, the macOS install is odd.

macos.c|libobjc or coregraphics is missi.what: The frameworks loaded but some function goome looks up at runtime isnt in them, which means the macOS version is older than goome supports. Comes from `goome_open`.
macos.c|libobjc or coregraphics is missi.fix: Update macOS. Goome says nothing about which symbol it was, so if updating isnt possible please report your macOS version.

macos.c|macos does overlay and window mo.what: You asked `goome_open` for a mode macOS doesnt support. Only the overlay and window modes exist here.

macos.c|appkit only works on the main th.what: `goome_open` was called from a thread that isnt the main thread, and AppKit refuses to create windows anywhere else. Goome also prints a line to stderr about it.
macos.c|appkit only works on the main th.fix: Call `goome_open` from the thread that runs `main()` and keep your own work on other threads.

macos.c|cant set up NSApplication.what: Goome couldnt get the shared `NSApplication` or register its helper classes with the Objective-C runtime. Comes from `goome_open` in overlay or window mode.
macos.c|cant set up NSApplication.fix: Not sure what makes this fail, its normally a broken session with no window server. Run it from a logged in desktop session and try again.

macos.c|macos says there are no displays.what: The overlay opened, but CoreGraphics returned an empty display list, so there is nothing to draw on. Comes from `goome_open` in overlay mode.
macos.c|macos says there are no displays.fix: Make sure a screen is on and youre in a graphical login session (not ssh or a screen locked at the login window). Then open again.

macos.c|no monitor <mon>.what: The monitor index `<mon>` isnt one goome knows about. Comes from `goome_capture` or from committing a canvas for a monitor that went away or never existed.
macos.c|no monitor <mon>.fix: Use an index below the monitor count that goome reports, and re-read it after you hear a monitor change since screens can come and go.

macos.c|the macos overlay isnt open.what: Screen grabs on macOS go through the overlay, and capture was opened with no overlay (or window) open before it. Comes from `goome_open` when it sets up capture.
macos.c|the macos overlay isnt open.fix: Open in overlay or window mode so goome has something to attach the capture to, then capture.

macos.c|screen grabs need macos 14 or ne.what: Screen capture uses `SCScreenshotManager` from ScreenCaptureKit and that class isnt on your system. It needs macOS 14 Sonoma or newer. Comes from `goome_open` with capture.
macos.c|screen grabs need macos 14 or ne.fix: Update to macOS 14 or newer. On older versions you can still use goome for overlays and windows, just not capture.

macos.c|macos wont let this app record t.what: Screen recording permission isnt granted, so macOS blocked the capture. Permission goes to the app that launched goome, so when you run from a terminal its the terminal that needs it. Goome already triggered the system prompt once. Comes from `goome_open`.
macos.c|macos wont let this app record t.fix: Turn on your terminal or app under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Screen & System Audio Recording. Then quit it fully and start it again, macOS only picks the change up on a fresh launch.

macos.c|screen recording got turned down.what: ScreenCaptureKit refused to list the screens with a permission error, so screen recording is denied for this app. Comes from `goome_open`.
macos.c|screen recording got turned down.fix: Allow the app (or your terminal) under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Screen & System Audio Recording, then restart it.

macos.c|screencapturekit didnt list the.what: ScreenCaptureKit failed to give goome the list of screens in 5 seconds, and `<n>` is the error code (-1 is a timeout). Comes from `goome_open`.
macos.c|screencapturekit didnt list the.fix: Try again, it can fail right at login or while the screen is waking. If it keeps happening, the `<n>` code is the thing to search for.

macos.c|screencapturekit doesnt know dis.what: ScreenCaptureKit doesnt list the display with id `<id>`, even after goome refreshed its list. That happens when a screen was just plugged or unplugged. Comes from `goome_capture`.
macos.c|screencapturekit doesnt know dis.fix: Wait a moment and call `goome_capture` again. If the monitor really is gone, stop grabbing from it.

macos.c|cant set up the screenshot.what: Goome couldnt allocate the objects it needs for a screenshot request (the content filter, config or state), so the grab never started. Comes from `goome_capture`.
macos.c|cant set up the screenshot.fix: This is a real out of memory, theres nothing the app can do except free some memory.

macos.c|screen recording got turned down.what: The screenshot call came back with the screen recording permission error, so macOS blocked this grab. That can happen if you took the permission away while goome was running. Comes from `goome_capture`.
macos.c|screen recording got turned down.fix: Allow the app (or your terminal) under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Screen & System Audio Recording, then restart it.

macos.c|the screenshot took over 2 s.what: ScreenCaptureKit didnt hand back an image within 2 seconds, so goome gave up on that grab. Comes from `goome_capture`.
macos.c|the screenshot took over 2 s.fix: Call it again, this is usually a busy system or a screen waking up. If it keeps timing out, grab a smaller rect or less often.

macos.c|the screenshot failed (error <n>.what: ScreenCaptureKit returned an error for the screenshot, and `<n>` is its code. Comes from `goome_capture`.
macos.c|the screenshot failed (error <n>.fix: Try the grab again, its often a screen changing mid grab. If one code keeps coming back, thats what to search for.

macos.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> grab.what: Goome couldnt allocate the buffer for a `<w>`x`<h>` capture. Comes from `goome_capture`.
macos.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> grab.fix: Grab a smaller rect or free up memory. Theres nothing else the app can do.

macos.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap.what: The screenshot came back, but goome couldnt create the CoreGraphics bitmap context of `<w>`x`<h>` to convert it to pixels. Comes from `goome_capture` and normally means the size is too big or memory is out.
macos.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap.fix: Grab a smaller rect. If it happens on small sizes too, the machine is low on memory.

macos.c|too many goome windows.what: You already have the most goome windows that goome tracks open at once, so `goome_open` in window mode wont make another.
macos.c|too many goome windows.fix: Close a window you dont need with `goome_close` before opening a new one.

macos.c|no memory for the window.what: Goome couldnt allocate its per window state, so the window mode `goome_open` failed.
macos.c|no memory for the window.fix: Thats a real out of memory, theres nothing the app can do except free some.

macos.c|cant make the NSWindow.what: AppKit returned nothing when goome tried to create the `NSWindow`. Comes from `goome_open` in window mode.
macos.c|cant make the NSWindow.fix: Not sure what makes AppKit do this, its usually a session with no window server. Check youre in a normal logged in desktop session and try again.

macos.c|cant make the window bitmap.what: The window was created but goome couldnt size its pixel buffer, either from a lack of memory or because the width or height ended up under 1 pixel. Comes from `goome_open` in window mode.
macos.c|cant make the window bitmap.fix: Pass a real width and height in the options (at least 1) and check youre not out of memory.

macos.c|the left button isnt down anymor.what: You asked for a window drag or resize with `goome_window_*`, but macOS says the left mouse button is already up, so there is nothing to drag. Usually the click ended before the call ran.
macos.c|the left button isnt down anymor.fix: Start the drag from the mouse down handler, while the button is still held. If you get this, just ignore it and wait for the next press.

macos.c|this window isnt resizable.what: You asked for a resize drag with a `goome_window_*` call on a window that wasnt opened with `GOOME_WINDOW_RESIZABLE`.
macos.c|this window isnt resizable.fix: Open the window with the `GOOME_WINDOW_RESIZABLE` flag, or only ask for moves.

macos.c|macos cant do window op <op>.what: A `goome_window_*` call asked for an operation (number `<op>`) that the macOS window code doesnt know.
macos.c|macos cant do window op <op>.fix: Use one of the window calls listed in the docs, on macOS only those are handled. Please report it if the call you used is in the docs.

macos.c|the window isnt on any display.what: To grab a window goome finds which display its center sits on, and the center isnt on any active display. Comes from `goome_capture` in window mode.
macos.c|the window isnt on any display.fix: Move the window onto a screen and grab again. It can also happen briefly while displays are changing, so retry.

macos.c|appkit isnt loaded.what: A `goome_clipboard_*` call ran before goome loaded AppKit, which happens when nothing has been opened yet or the load failed.
macos.c|appkit isnt loaded.fix: Call `goome_open` first (it has to succeed) and then use the clipboard.

macos.c|no NSPasteboardTypeString here.what: AppKit loaded but doesnt export the plain text pasteboard type goome needs for `goome_clipboard_get` or `goome_clipboard_set`. Thats a very old or odd macOS.
macos.c|no NSPasteboardTypeString here.fix: Update macOS. Not sure how else you could hit this on a normal install.

macos.c|that text isnt utf-8.what: `goome_clipboard_set` was given a string macOS couldnt read as UTF-8, so nothing was copied.
macos.c|that text isnt utf-8.fix: Pass valid UTF-8 text with a terminating zero.

macos.c|the pasteboard didnt take it.what: macOS accepted the call but `setString:forType:` returned no, so the text wasnt put on the clipboard. From `goome_clipboard_set`.
macos.c|the pasteboard didnt take it.fix: Try again. Not sure why the pasteboard says no, it can happen if another app is holding it or the session is locked.

macos.c|no memory for the clipboard.what: `goome_clipboard_get` found text on the clipboard but couldnt allocate a copy of it.
macos.c|no memory for the clipboard.fix: Thats a real out of memory, theres nothing the app can do except free some.

image.c|image size out of range.what: A decoder asked for a bitmap with a width or height of 0 or more than 16384 pixels, so `goome_bitmap_load` or `goome_bitmap_load_mem` refused to allocate it.
image.c|image size out of range.fix: The file is probably lying about its size. Open it in an image editor, shrink it to 16384 pixels or less per side and save it again.

image.c|out of memory.what: `malloc` or `calloc` failed while goome was loading the image, either for the file buffer, the pixel buffer or a decoder work buffer. Big images need a lot, a 16384 by 16384 one is 1 GB of pixels alone.
image.c|out of memory.fix: Nothing goome can do about a real out of memory. Free some RAM or load a smaller image, and scale huge files down before loading.

image.c|png has no header.what: The png has its signature but the first chunk isnt a proper `IHDR` (or its shorter than 13 bytes), or no `IHDR` showed up at all. Comes back from `goome_bitmap_load` or `goome_bitmap_load_mem`.
image.c|png has no header.fix: The file is damaged or isnt really a png. Open and export it again from an image editor, or convert it with `convert in.png out.png`.

image.c|png size out of range.what: The png header says the width or height is 0 or bigger than 16384, which goome wont decode.
image.c|png size out of range.fix: Resize the image to 16384 pixels or less on each side. If the size looks absurd for your file, the header is damaged, so export it again.

image.c|png header has a bad color type.what: The `IHDR` has a color type and bit depth combo that png doesnt allow, or non zero compression/filter bytes, or an interlace value above 1.
image.c|png header has a bad color type.fix: The file is broken or was written by a buggy tool. Export it again as a normal 8 bit png from an image editor.

image.c|png palette missing.what: The png says it is a palette image (color type 3) but never has a `PLTE` chunk, so goome has no colors to look up.
image.c|png palette missing.fix: Re-save the image from an editor, or convert it to a plain RGB png so it doesnt need a palette.

image.c|png has no image data.what: The png header was fine but there is no `IDAT` data (or its basically empty) after it, so theres no pixels to read. Often a file that got cut off while copying or downloading.
image.c|png has no image data.fix: Download or copy the file again and compare its size. If its really like that, export the image again.

image.c|png too big to decode.what: The unpacked pixel data of this png would be over 2 GB, so goome gives up before it tries. Large interlaced images get there fast.
image.c|png too big to decode.fix: Scale the image down in an editor and save it again. Theres no setting to raise the limit.

image.c|png data is not zlib.what: The `IDAT` data doesnt start with a valid zlib header (wrong method, window size or it asks for a preset dictionary), so it cant be unpacked.
image.c|png data is not zlib.fix: The png is damaged or made by a weird encoder. Open it in an image editor and export it again, or run it through `optipng` or `pngcrush`.

image.c|png data is corrupt or cut off.what: Unpacking the png pixel data ran out of input or hit invalid compressed data before it got all the rows. Usually a truncated download or a damaged file.
image.c|png data is corrupt or cut off.fix: Get a fresh copy of the file. If the original is the same, export the png again from an editor.

image.c|png has a bad filter type.what: One of the png rows uses a filter byte above 4, which isnt a real png filter. The compressed data decoded but the content is garbage.
image.c|png has a bad filter type.fix: The file is corrupt. Replace it with a good copy or export it again from an image editor.

image.c|jpeg is too short for its size.what: The jpeg header claims far more image than the file has bytes to hold, so goome stops before allocating buffers. Normally a truncated file or a header with a bogus size.
image.c|jpeg is too short for its size.fix: Get the file again in full. If it still fails, open it in an editor that can recover it and save a new jpeg, or convert it to png.

image.c|progressive jpeg too big to deco.what: This is a progressive jpeg and storing all its coefficients would take more than goome allows, so it wont decode it.
image.c|progressive jpeg too big to deco.fix: Save it as a baseline (non progressive) jpeg or shrink it in an editor. Converting to png also works.

image.c|jpeg scan before frame.what: The jpeg has a scan (`SOS` marker) before any frame header (`SOF`), so goome doesnt know the size or components yet. Thats not a valid order.
image.c|jpeg scan before frame.fix: The file is damaged or hand edited. Export it again from an image editor.

image.c|jpeg scan header cut off.what: The jpeg scan header segment is empty, so the file ends in the middle of it.
image.c|jpeg scan header cut off.fix: Likely a truncated file. Fetch it again, or open and re-save it in an image editor.

image.c|jpeg scan header is bad.what: The scan header has a component count outside 1 to 4, or its shorter than that count needs.
image.c|jpeg scan header is bad.fix: The jpeg is corrupt. Re-export it from an editor, or convert to png and load that.

image.c|jpeg scan uses a missing compone.what: A scan points at a component id that the frame header never defined. goome cant tell which color channel it belongs to.
image.c|jpeg scan uses a missing compone.fix: The file is broken or from a strange encoder. Re-save it in an image editor to get a clean jpeg.

image.c|jpeg scan repeats a component.what: The same color component is listed twice in one scan header, which jpeg doesnt allow.
image.c|jpeg scan repeats a component.fix: The file is corrupt. Export it again from an editor or convert it to png.

image.c|jpeg progressive scan is bad.what: A scan in this progressive jpeg has spectral selection or successive approximation values that dont make sense (like a bad start/end band or refinement bits).
image.c|jpeg progressive scan is bad.fix: The jpeg is damaged or made by a buggy encoder. Re-export it as baseline jpeg or png.

image.c|jpeg huffman table missing.what: A scan needs a huffman table that no `DHT` segment ever defined, so goome cant decode the compressed data.
image.c|jpeg huffman table missing.fix: Some odd jpegs (like old mjpeg frames) rely on default tables and goome doesnt supply them. Re-save the image from an editor so the tables get written.

image.c|jpeg quant table missing.what: A scan uses a quantization table that no `DQT` segment defined, so the values cant be scaled back.
image.c|jpeg quant table missing.fix: The file is incomplete or damaged. Re-save it from an image editor or convert to png.

image.c|jpeg mcu too big.what: The jpeg has a block layout where one MCU holds more than 10 blocks across its components, which the spec doesnt allow.
image.c|jpeg mcu too big.fix: The sampling factors in the header are wrong, so the file is broken. Export it again from an editor.

image.c|jpeg has two frames.what: The jpeg has a second frame header (`SOF`) after the first one. goome only handles a single frame per file.
image.c|jpeg has two frames.fix: Re-save the image from an editor to get a plain single frame jpeg. A file thats several images glued together needs to be split first.

image.c|jpeg frame header cut off.what: The jpeg frame header is shorter than the 6 bytes it needs at the minimum, so the file ends or is damaged there.
image.c|jpeg frame header cut off.fix: Download or copy it again. If its still the same, re-export the image.

image.c|only 8 bit jpeg is supported.what: The jpeg uses a sample precision other than 8 bits, like a 12 bit medical or scientific jpeg, and goome only decodes 8 bit.
image.c|only 8 bit jpeg is supported.fix: Convert it to an 8 bit jpeg or a png with an image tool such as `convert in.jpg -depth 8 out.png`.

image.c|jpeg with the height in a dnl ma.what: The jpeg header has a height of 0, which means the real height comes later in a `DNL` marker. goome doesnt read that.
image.c|jpeg with the height in a dnl ma.fix: Re-save it from an image editor so the height is in the normal header. Its a rare format so most editors will fix it just by opening and exporting.

image.c|jpeg size out of range.what: The jpeg has a width of 0, or a width or height above 16384.
image.c|jpeg size out of range.fix: Shrink the image in an editor and save it again. If the size shown is nonsense for the picture, the header is damaged.

image.c|jpeg frame header is bad.what: The frame header has a bad component count (not 1 to 4), a sampling factor outside 1 to 4, a quant table id above 3, or its too short for the components it lists.
image.c|jpeg frame header is bad.fix: The jpeg is corrupt. Open and save it again in an image editor, or convert it to png.

image.c|jpeg too big to decode.what: The decoded planes for this jpeg would take more than 2 GB, so goome refuses.
image.c|jpeg too big to decode.fix: Make the picture smaller before loading, with an editor or `convert in.jpg -resize 50% out.jpg`.

image.c|jpeg segment cut off.what: A jpeg marker segment says its longer than whats left in the file (or shorter than its own length bytes) before any scan was read.
image.c|jpeg segment cut off.fix: The file is truncated or damaged. Get a full copy, or export it again from an editor.

image.c|hierarchical jpeg is not support.what: The jpeg uses the hierarchical (differential) mode, which goome has no decoder for.
image.c|hierarchical jpeg is not support.fix: Its very rare. Open it in an image editor and save as normal jpeg or png.

image.c|arithmetic coded jpeg is not sup.what: The jpeg uses arithmetic coding instead of huffman coding. goome only decodes huffman jpegs.
image.c|arithmetic coded jpeg is not sup.fix: Re-save it as a standard huffman jpeg, for example with `jpegtran` or an image editor, or convert to png.

image.c|lossless jpeg is not supported.what: The file is a lossless jpeg (the old jpeg-ls style process), not the usual lossy one, and goome cant decode it.
image.c|lossless jpeg is not supported.fix: Convert it to png with an image tool and load that instead.

image.c|jpeg huffman table is bad.what: A huffman table segment has a bad class or id, too many codes or runs past the end of the segment, or the code lengths dont add up to a valid table.
image.c|jpeg huffman table is bad.fix: The jpeg is corrupt. Export it again from an editor or convert to png.

image.c|jpeg quant table is bad.what: A quantization table segment has a bad precision or id, or its shorter than the 64 values it should hold.
image.c|jpeg quant table is bad.fix: The file is damaged. Re-save it from an image editor.

image.c|jpeg has too many scans.what: The jpeg has 256 or more scans, way past anything normal. A progressive jpeg usually has about 10.
image.c|jpeg has too many scans.fix: The file is broken or built to be nasty. Re-export it from an editor or convert to png.

image.c|jpeg has no image data.what: goome went through the whole jpeg and never found a frame header or a scan, so there was nothing to decode.
image.c|jpeg has no image data.fix: The file is empty after the header, truncated or only has metadata. Get the full file or export it again.

image.c|bmp cut off.what: The bmp ends before where its own header says the pixel data (or palette and bitfield masks) should be. Typical for a half downloaded file.
image.c|bmp cut off.fix: Get the file again. If it keeps happening, open it in an editor and save a fresh bmp or png.

image.c|bmp header is bad.what: The bmp info header size is under 40 and not the old 12 byte kind, or it claims to be bigger than the file.
image.c|bmp header is bad.fix: The header is damaged or the file isnt a real bmp. Export it again from an image editor, or convert it to png.

image.c|bmp size out of range.what: The bmp has a width of 0 or less, a height of 0, or a size above 16384 pixels.
image.c|bmp size out of range.fix: Resize the image to 16384 or less on each side and save it again. A negative width means the header is damaged.

image.c|rle bmp is not supported.what: The bmp is compressed with RLE4 or RLE8. goome only reads uncompressed and bitfield bmps.
image.c|rle bmp is not supported.fix: Save it again as an uncompressed bmp, or just use png.

image.c|bmp with jpeg or png inside is n.what: This bmp has a jpeg or png stream wrapped inside it (compression type 4 or 5), which goome doesnt unwrap.
image.c|bmp with jpeg or png inside is n.fix: Open it in an image editor and export as a plain bmp, or save the picture as png or jpeg directly.

image.c|bmp compression is unknown.what: The bmp compression field is a number goome doesnt know, so it cant say how the pixels are stored. Often the header is damaged.
image.c|bmp compression is unknown.fix: Re-export the bmp from an editor, or convert it to png.

image.c|bmp bit depth is bad.what: The bmp bits per pixel is something other than 1, 4, 8, 16, 24 or 32.
image.c|bmp bit depth is bad.fix: The header is damaged or its a rare format. Save it again as a 24 bit bmp or a png.

image.c|bmp bitfields need 16 or 32 bit.what: The bmp has channel masks (bitfields compression) but its bit depth isnt 16 or 32, which makes no sense.
image.c|bmp bitfields need 16 or 32 bit.fix: Re-export it from an image editor as a normal 24 bit bmp, or convert to png.

image.c|only binary ppm, pgm and pbm are.what: The file starts with `P1`, `P2`, `P3` or `P7`, so its a plain text netpbm or a pam. goome only reads the binary ones (`P4`, `P5`, `P6`).
image.c|only binary ppm, pgm and pbm are.fix: Convert it to a binary one with `pnmtopnm` from netpbm, or just save it as png.

image.c|ppm header is bad.what: goome couldnt read the width, height or maxval numbers in the netpbm header. They are missing, not numbers or too large.
image.c|ppm header is bad.fix: Check the header looks like `P6 width height 255` with a whitespace between each. Re-export it from an editor if not.

image.c|ppm cut off.what: The netpbm file ends right after the header, or it has fewer pixel bytes than width times height says it needs.
image.c|ppm cut off.fix: Get the file again, or re-export it. A file missing its tail often comes from an interrupted write.

image.c|ppm size out of range.what: The ppm, pgm or pbm has a width or height of 0 or above 16384.
image.c|ppm size out of range.fix: Resize the image so each side is 16384 pixels or less and save it again.

image.c|ppm maxval is bad.what: The maxval in the netpbm header is 0 or above 65535, which the format doesnt allow.
image.c|ppm maxval is bad.fix: The header is wrong. Re-export the file from a tool that writes a standard 255 maxval.

image.c|qoi cut off.what: The qoi data ends too early, either before the 14 byte header or in the middle of the pixel stream before all pixels were read.
image.c|qoi cut off.fix: The file is truncated. Get it again or convert it from the source image with a qoi tool.

image.c|qoi size out of range.what: The qoi header gives a width or height of 0 or above 16384.
image.c|qoi size out of range.fix: Resize the original and encode it as qoi again. If the size looks silly the header is damaged.

image.c|qoi header is bad.what: The qoi header says the channel count is something other than 3 or 4.
image.c|qoi header is bad.fix: The file is damaged or was written by a broken encoder. Encode it again, or use png.

image.c|qoi is too short for its size.what: The qoi header claims more pixels than the data could possibly hold, even if it was all runs, so goome stops early.
image.c|qoi is too short for its size.fix: The size in the header is wrong or the file is cut. Make a new qoi from the source image.

image.c|no bitmap given.what: You passed a null `goome_bitmap *out` to `goome_bitmap_load` or `goome_bitmap_load_mem`, so theres nowhere to put the result.
image.c|no bitmap given.fix: Pass a pointer to a `goome_bitmap` you own. Its a bug in your code, not in the image.

image.c|no data given.fix: Pass a real buffer with the file bytes in it and its length in `n`.

image.c|gif is not supported.what: The data starts with `GIF87a` or `GIF89a`, so it is a gif and goome doesnt decode those.
image.c|gif is not supported.fix: Convert it to png first, for example `convert in.gif[0] out.png` for the first frame.

image.c|webp is not supported.what: The data is a `RIFF`/`WEBP` file and goome has no webp decoder.
image.c|webp is not supported.fix: Convert it to png or jpeg with `dwebp` or an image editor.

image.c|unknown image format.what: The first bytes dont match png, jpeg, bmp, qoi, ppm, pgm or pbm. The file might be another format like tiff or svg, or not an image at all, or empty.
image.c|unknown image format.fix: Check what the file really is with `file name`, then convert it to png. A bad download that saved an html error page does this a lot.

image.c|no path given.fix: Pass the path to the image file as a utf-8 string.

image.c|cant open the file.what: `goome_bitmap_load` couldnt open the path for reading, because it doesnt exist, you dont have permission, or the path is wrong. Goome doesnt tell which one.
image.c|cant open the file.fix: Check the path (relative paths start from the working directory of the app), and that your user can read the file.

image.c|file is bigger than 256 MB.what: The file you gave `goome_bitmap_load` is over the 256 MB size limit, so goome stopped reading it.
image.c|file is bigger than 256 MB.fix: Use a smaller image. If you really need a huge one, shrink it or convert it to a more compact format like png.

image.c|cant read the file.what: The file opened fine but reading it hit an error partway through. Could be a directory instead of a file, a flaky drive or a network share dropping out.
image.c|cant read the file.fix: Check the path is a regular file and copy it somewhere local to try again.

wl.c|cant find libwayland-client.so.0.what: `goome_open` tried to `dlopen` `libwayland-client.so.0` for wayland and the system doesnt have it.
wl.c|cant find libwayland-client.so.0.fix: Install the wayland client library (`libwayland-client0` on Debian and Ubuntu, `wayland` on Arch, `libwayland-client` on Fedora). If youre on X11 this shouldnt come up, so check your session type.

wl.c|libwayland-client.so.0 has no <symb.what: The wayland library was found but its missing the function `<symbol>`, which goome needs. Libraries older than 1.20 usually lack `wl_proxy_marshal_flags`.
wl.c|libwayland-client.so.0 has no <symb.fix: Update `libwayland-client` to 1.20 or newer, which any current distro ships.

wl.c|WAYLAND_DISPLAY isnt set.what: `goome_open` picked the wayland backend but neither `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` nor `WAYLAND_SOCKET` is in the environment, so theres no compositor to talk to.
wl.c|WAYLAND_DISPLAY isnt set.fix: Run the app from inside your wayland session, not over plain ssh or a bare tty. Under sudo or a service, pass `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` through.

wl.c|cant connect to the wayland display.what: `wl_display_connect` failed for the socket named in `<wayland_display>`. Usually the socket doesnt exist or your user cant reach it.
wl.c|cant connect to the wayland display.fix: Check that `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<wayland_display>` exists and is yours. Wrong `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` after su or sudo is the usual cause.

wl.c|the wayland display hung up on us.what: The compositor closed the connection while goome was setting up, or a round trip to it failed. `goome_open` returns this, in window mode too.
wl.c|the wayland display hung up on us.fix: Try again, and check the compositor didnt crash. Its not clear from the code why a compositor would drop a fresh client, so the compositor log is the place to look.

wl.c|this compositor has no wl_composito.what: The compositor connected fine but didnt offer the two basic globals goome needs to draw anything. `goome_open` gives this back in overlay and window mode.
wl.c|this compositor has no wl_composito.fix: Thats very unusual for a normal desktop compositor. Check that youre really connecting to a full compositor and not a stripped down or nested one.

wl.c|wayland does overlay and window mod.what: `goome_open` on wayland was given a mode other than `GOOME_MODE_OVERLAY` or `GOOME_MODE_WINDOW`. `GOOME_MODE_OFFSCREEN` isnt handled by this backend.
wl.c|wayland does overlay and window mod.fix: Use overlay or window mode for `opts.mode`. For offscreen, pick a backend that supports it.

wl.c|this compositor has no layer-shell.what: Overlay mode on wayland needs the wlr layer-shell protocol and this compositor doesnt offer it. GNOME and its Mutter compositor are the common ones without it.
wl.c|this compositor has no layer-shell.fix: Use `GOOME_MODE_WINDOW` instead, or run on a compositor with layer-shell like Hyprland, Sway or KDE.

wl.c|the compositor didnt tell me about.what: The overlay opened but the compositor never reported a monitor, so goome has nothing to put layers on. `goome_open` returns this.
wl.c|the compositor didnt tell me about.fix: Check that a monitor is actually enabled and connected, then try again. Not sure what makes a compositor report zero outputs other than all of them being off or still starting up.

wl.c|monitor <mon> is gone.what: The monitor index `<mon>` doesnt match a live output any more, usually because it was unplugged or the layout changed. Shows up from the overlay commit and from `goome_capture`.
wl.c|monitor <mon> is gone.fix: Re-read the monitor list with the goome monitor calls and use a current index. Drop any canvas you were holding for the old one.

wl.c|out of memory for <n> hit rects.what: A `malloc` failed while storing the `<n>` click-through rectangles for an overlay commit.
wl.c|out of memory for <n> hit rects.fix: Nothing the app can do about a real out of memory. If `<n>` is huge, send fewer hit rects.

wl.c|wayland: no layer surface to take t.what: `goome_grab` with on set was called but there are no live layer surfaces to give keyboard focus to, and wayland has no way to grab the pointer by itself.
wl.c|wayland: no layer surface to take t.fix: Make sure the overlay is open and its monitors are up before grabbing. Without a layer surface theres no fallback, so skip the grab.

wl.c|the compositor never configured the.what: goome made the window and waited about 20 round trips for the compositor to send its first configure, which never came. `goome_open` in window mode returns this.
wl.c|the compositor never configured the.fix: Check the compositors xdg-shell support is working and try again. Not sure why a compositor would stay silent here, so look at its log.

wl.c|out of memory for the window.what: Building the windows shared memory buffer failed right after the window was configured. This can also mean the compositor refused the shm pool.
wl.c|out of memory for the window.fix: If its a real out of memory theres nothing to do. Otherwise try a smaller `width` and `height`, and check `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is writable and has space.

wl.c|out of memory.what: `goome_open` in window mode couldnt allocate the window state struct.
wl.c|out of memory.fix: Nothing the app can do, the machine is out of memory.

wl.c|this compositor has no xdg-shell, c.what: Window mode needs `xdg_wm_base` and the compositor didnt list it, so goome cant make a normal window.
wl.c|this compositor has no xdg-shell, c.fix: Use a compositor that supports xdg-shell, which is nearly all of them. `GOOME_MODE_OVERLAY` is the other option if it has layer-shell.

wl.c|wayland doesnt let apps see or set.what: `goome_window_pos` was called on a wayland window, and the protocol hides and forbids window positions.
wl.c|wayland doesnt let apps see or set.fix: Dont rely on window position on wayland. Check for `GOOME_ENOTSUP` and skip it, or center the window by letting the compositor place it.

wl.c|the window is hidden.what: A window state change like maximize or fullscreen was asked for but the toplevel doesnt exist right now, because the window was hidden.
wl.c|the window is hidden.fix: Show it again with `goome_window_show(g, 1)` first, then change its state.

wl.c|no mouse button is down.what: A window drag or resize was asked for but goome has no mouse button held or no press serial. Wayland only lets a move or resize start from a real press.
wl.c|no mouse button is down.fix: Call the drag from your mouse down handler while the button is still held, not later from a timer.

wl.c|this compositor has no clipboard (w.what: `goome_clipboard_set` found no `wl_data_device_manager` or data device on the compositor, so theres no clipboard to write to.
wl.c|this compositor has no clipboard (w.fix: Use a compositor that offers the data device protocol, which normal desktops do. Nothing to change in your app.

wl.c|wayland only lets a window set the.what: `goome_clipboard_set` needs a serial from a recent click or key press in the window and goome hasnt seen one yet.
wl.c|wayland only lets a window set the.fix: Set the clipboard from inside a click or key handler, after the user has interacted with the window.

wl.c|cant make a pipe.what: `pipe()` failed while reading the clipboard in `goome_clipboard_get`, so goome couldnt receive the data.
wl.c|cant make a pipe.fix: Your process is probably out of file descriptors. Close ones you dont need or raise the `ulimit -n`.

wl.c|the app that owns the clipboard did.what: `goome_clipboard_get` asked the app that owns the clipboard for its text and got nothing back within about 250 ms.
wl.c|the app that owns the clipboard did.fix: Try again. The owning app might be frozen or slow, and goome cant tell which.

wl.c|this compositor has no wlr-screenco.what: The compositor doesnt offer `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1`, so `goome_capture` has no way to read the screen. GNOME and KDE dont ship it.
wl.c|this compositor has no wlr-screenco.fix: Use a wlroots based compositor like Sway or Hyprland, or capture some other way on this desktop.

wl.c|lost the wayland display.what: The connection to the compositor broke while goome waited for a screen grab to finish. `goome_capture` returns this.
wl.c|lost the wayland display.fix: The compositor probably crashed or quit, so reopen goome once its back.

wl.c|monitor <mon> got unplugged.what: The output for `<mon>` disappeared in the middle of a `goome_capture`.
wl.c|monitor <mon> got unplugged.fix: Refresh your monitor list and grab again with a current index.

wl.c|<name> never sent a frame (asleep?).what: `goome_capture` asked output `<name>` for a frame and nothing came within 600 ms. Most often the screen is off or asleep.
wl.c|<name> never sent a frame (asleep?).fix: Wake the display and try again, retrying a bit later works too.

wl.c|<name> only offers screen formats i.what: The compositor offered only pixel formats for output `<name>` that goome cant convert, and `<list>` shows which ones.
wl.c|<name> only offers screen formats i.fix: Not much to do from your app. If `<list>` is a common format, tell me so I can add it.

wl.c|the compositor wont let me grab <na.what: The screencopy frame for `<name>` failed. goome also uses this when it couldnt make the shared buffer for the frame, so I cant say which from the error alone.
wl.c|the compositor wont let me grab <na.fix: Try again. Some compositors refuse protected or hidden outputs, so check their settings and log.

wl.c|out of memory for a <w>x<h> grab.what: `malloc` failed for the pixel buffer of a `<w>x<h>` `goome_capture`, or the output reported a zero size.
wl.c|out of memory for a <w>x<h> grab.fix: If it really is out of memory theres nothing to do. Grab a smaller region instead of the whole screen.

win32.c|win32 does overlay and window mo.what: `goome_open` on Windows only knows `GOOME_MODE_OVERLAY` and `GOOME_MODE_WINDOW`, and you passed some other mode.
win32.c|win32 does overlay and window mo.fix: Pick one of those two modes in the options you hand to `goome_open`.

win32.c|cant load gdi32.dll.what: goome loads `gdi32.dll` itself to draw, and Windows wouldnt give it to us when `goome_open` ran in overlay or window mode. This is rare and usually means a badly broken or stripped down Windows install.
win32.c|cant load gdi32.dll.fix: Check the machine is a normal desktop Windows and that `C:\Windows\System32\gdi32.dll` exists. Running `sfc /scannow` can fix a damaged system.

win32.c|cant register the overlay window.what: `goome_open` in overlay mode asked Windows to register its `goome_overlay` window class and Windows said no. `<error>` is the Win32 `GetLastError` number.
win32.c|cant register the overlay window.fix: Look the number up to see why. Most often a leftover class from a crashed run in the same process or a locked down session, so restart the app.

win32.c|windows says there are no monito.what: `goome_open` in overlay mode asked Windows for the monitor list and got nothing back. Usually its a session with no display attached, like a service or a remote session that isnt active.
win32.c|windows says there are no monito.fix: Run the app in a normal logged in desktop session with a screen on.

win32.c|cant make the overlay window on.what: `goome_open` made the overlay window for monitor `<name>` and `CreateWindowEx` failed. `<error>` is the Win32 error number.
win32.c|cant make the overlay window on.fix: Look up the error number. Out of window handles or a restricted desktop are the usual reasons, so close some apps or run on the normal desktop.

win32.c|no memory for <n> hit rects.what: goome couldnt grow its list of `<n>` click-through hit rects while committing a frame, so the overlay or transparent window didnt update.
win32.c|no memory for <n> hit rects.fix: Thats a real out of memory, nothing the app can do except free some RAM. If `<n>` is huge, pass fewer hit rects.

win32.c|windows wont hand us the keyboar.what: Asking for the keyboard (`goome_keyboard` or a pointer grab that needs it) made goome call `SetForegroundWindow`, and Windows refused because another app owns the foreground focus lock.
win32.c|windows wont hand us the keyboar.fix: Have the user click the overlay first so it gets focus, then ask for the keyboard again. Doing it from a click or hotkey handler works best.

win32.c|no overlay window to hold the po.what: A pointer grab was asked for but goome couldnt find an overlay window to capture the mouse with, so there was nothing to hold it.
win32.c|no overlay window to hold the po.fix: Grab the pointer while the overlay is visible, like inside a click handler on it. Make sure `goome_open` succeeded first.

win32.c|another app already has the hotk.what: `goome_hotkey` couldnt register the hotkey with id `<id>` because Windows says another app already took that key combo. If several failed, this names the last one.
win32.c|another app already has the hotk.fix: Pick a different key or modifiers for that hotkey, or close the other app. Adding `GOOME_SHIFT` or `GOOME_CTRL` often gets around a clash.

win32.c|the key for hotkey id <id> isnt.what: `goome_hotkey` couldnt turn the key for hotkey id `<id>` into a Windows virtual key, because the current keyboard layout has no such key. If several failed, this names the last one.
win32.c|the key for hotkey id <id> isnt.fix: Use a key that exists on every layout, like a letter, a digit or an F key. Or check the layout the user has active.

win32.c|cant turn that text into utf-16.what: Windows wouldnt convert the text you gave `goome_clipboard_set` from utf-8 to utf-16, which usually means the string isnt valid utf-8.
win32.c|cant turn that text into utf-16.fix: Pass valid utf-8 text. If it comes from a file or bytes, clean or re-encode it first.

win32.c|no memory for the clipboard.what: goome ran out of memory building or reading the clipboard text, in `goome_clipboard_set` or `goome_clipboard_get`.
win32.c|no memory for the clipboard.fix: Thats a real out of memory, nothing the app can do except free some RAM or use less text.

win32.c|another app has the clipboard op.what: The clipboard was held open by another app and still was after goome retried for about 100 ms, so `goome_clipboard_set` or `goome_clipboard_get` gave up.
win32.c|another app has the clipboard op.fix: Just try the call again in a moment. Clipboard managers and remote desktop tools hold it open a lot.

win32.c|windows wont take the clipboard.what: `goome_clipboard_set` opened the clipboard but `SetClipboardData` failed. `<error>` is the Win32 error number.
win32.c|windows wont take the clipboard.fix: Look up the error number. Its rare, retrying once usually works, and a clipboard tool grabbing it at the same time can cause it.

win32.c|cant register the window class (.what: `goome_open` in window mode asked Windows to register its `goome_window` class and Windows said no. `<error>` is the Win32 `GetLastError` number.
win32.c|cant register the window class (.fix: Look the number up to see why. Restarting the app clears a leftover class, and a locked down session can also block it.

win32.c|no memory for the window.what: `goome_open` in window mode couldnt allocate its window state.
win32.c|no memory for the window.fix: Thats a real out of memory, nothing the app can do except free some RAM.

win32.c|cant make the window (error <err.what: `goome_open` in window mode failed at `CreateWindowEx`, or at making the device context it draws with. `<error>` is the Win32 error number, and it may be 0 if the device context was the problem.
win32.c|cant make the window (error <err.fix: Look up the error number. Out of GDI or window handles is the usual cause, so close other apps or check for a handle leak in yours.

win32.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap for t.what: `goome_open` in window mode couldnt make the `<w>x<h>` pixel buffer for the window, or Windows reported no monitors. Most likely the size is too big for memory, or the options have a bad width or height.
win32.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap for t.fix: Use a smaller `width` and `height` in the options, and check there is a monitor on the session.

win32.c|windows wont hand us the keyboar.what: Asking for the keyboard in window mode made goome call `SetForegroundWindow` and Windows refused because another app holds the focus lock.
win32.c|windows wont hand us the keyboar.fix: Have the user click the window first, then ask again. Calling it from a click or key handler works best.

win32.c|edges <edges> dont make a side o.what: `goome_window_drag` got an `<edges>` value that isnt a single side or a corner, like left and right together.
win32.c|edges <edges> dont make a side o.fix: Pass 0 to move the window, or one side or a corner like left, top or bottom-right as edge flags.

win32.c|this window isnt resizable.what: `goome_window_drag` was asked to resize by an edge but the window was opened without the resizable flag.
win32.c|this window isnt resizable.fix: Open it with `GOOME_WINDOW_RESIZABLE`, or pass edges 0 to move it instead.

win32.c|the left button isnt down anymor.what: `goome_window_drag` needs the left mouse button held, and it was already released by the time the call ran.
win32.c|the left button isnt down anymor.fix: Start the drag from the mouse down event right away and dont wait. If it fails, just skip it, the user let go.

win32.c|the window is gone.what: `goome_window_*` asked Windows for the window position and the window handle was dead, so the window was already destroyed.
win32.c|the window is gone.fix: Dont use the window after closing it or after the user shut it. Check for the close event first.

win32.c|win32 cant do window op <op>.what: A window call reached goome for an operation number `<op>` that the win32 window backend doesnt handle.
win32.c|win32 cant do window op <op>.fix: Use only the documented `goome_window_*` calls. If you did, its a goome bug, so please report it with the op number.

win32.c|that rect is off the window.what: `goome_capture` with a rect that lands completely outside the window, so there was nothing to grab. Its checked after clamping to the window size.
win32.c|that rect is off the window.fix: Pass a rect that overlaps the window, in window coordinates.

win32.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap to gr.what: `goome_capture` couldnt make the `<w>x<h>` pixel buffer it copies the screen into for the window.
win32.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap to gr.fix: Thats usually a real out of memory or out of GDI handles. Free some, or use a smaller window.

win32.c|BitBlt from the screen failed (e.what: `goome_capture` of a window failed in `BitBlt` copying from the screen. Usually the desktop is locked or showing UAC or the secure desktop, where Windows blocks grabs.
win32.c|BitBlt from the screen failed (e.fix: Unlock the desktop and try again, theres no way around the secure desktop. If not, check the Win32 `<error>` number.

win32.c|the window isnt open.what: `goome_capture` was started in window mode before the window had been opened with `goome_open`.
win32.c|the window isnt open.fix: Call `goome_open` first and check it worked, then open capture.

win32.c|win32 capture needs the win32 ov.what: `goome_capture` was started in overlay mode without the win32 overlay open, so the gdi library goome copies the screen with wasnt loaded.
win32.c|win32 capture needs the win32 ov.fix: Call `goome_open` in overlay mode and check it succeeded before capturing, and use the same mode for both.

win32.c|no monitor <mon>.what: `goome_capture` was asked for monitor `<mon>` and theres no such monitor index, maybe one got unplugged.
win32.c|no monitor <mon>.fix: Use an index below the monitor count you get from goome. Recheck after a monitor change.

win32.c|that rect is off monitor <mon>.what: `goome_capture` was given a rect that sits completely outside monitor `<mon>`, so there was nothing to grab.
win32.c|that rect is off monitor <mon>.fix: Pass a rect inside that monitors area, in the same coordinates the overlay uses.

win32.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap to gr.what: `goome_capture` couldnt make the `<w>x<h>` pixel buffer to copy monitor `<name>` into.
win32.c|cant make a <w>x<h> bitmap to gr.fix: Thats usually a real out of memory or out of GDI handles. Free some, nothing else the app can do.

win32.c|BitBlt from the screen failed on.what: `goome_capture` of monitor `<name>` failed in `BitBlt` copying from the screen. Usually the desktop is locked or showing UAC or the secure desktop, where Windows blocks grabs.
win32.c|BitBlt from the screen failed on.fix: Unlock the desktop and try again, theres no way around the secure desktop. If not, check the Win32 `<error>` number.

x11.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> overlay.what: The X11 overlay couldnt allocate its `<w>`x`<h>` pixel buffer while `goome_open` was setting up or after the screen size changed.
x11.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> overlay.fix: This is a real out of memory, theres nothing to change in the app. If the numbers look huge, check that the X server is reporting a sane screen size.

x11.c|XCreateImage failed for <w>x<h>.what: Xlib refused to wrap the overlay buffer in an image for a `<w>`x`<h>` screen, so the overlay couldnt be built. It comes from `goome_open` or from a later screen size change.
x11.c|XCreateImage failed for <w>x<h>.fix: Usually means Xlib itself ran out of memory, so free some up and try again. If it keeps happening on a normal screen size, thats a bug, tell me the resolution.

x11.c|x11 does overlay and window mode o.what: You asked `goome_open` for a mode the X11 backend doesnt have. It only does overlay and window.
x11.c|x11 does overlay and window mode o.fix: Use `GOOME_MODE_OVERLAY` or `GOOME_MODE_WINDOW` in the options when youre on X11.

x11.c|DISPLAY isnt set, no X server to t.what: `goome_open` (overlay or window mode) found no `DISPLAY` environment variable, so it has no X server to connect to.
x11.c|DISPLAY isnt set, no X server to t.fix: Run the app from inside a desktop session, or set `DISPLAY` (like `:0`). Over ssh or from a service the variable is usually missing.

x11.c|cant connect to the X server on <d.what: Xlib couldnt open the display named in `DISPLAY`, from `goome_open` or `goome_capture`. The server isnt running there or youre not allowed to use it.
x11.c|cant connect to the X server on <d.fix: Check that `DISPLAY` points at a live X server and that your user is allowed on it (`XAUTHORITY` for a different user, or `xhost`). On Wayland make sure XWayland is running.

x11.c|the X server has no XFixes, cant m.what: Overlay mode needs the XFixes extension to let mouse clicks pass through the overlay, and this X server doesnt have it. Comes from `goome_open`.
x11.c|the X server has no XFixes, cant m.fix: Use an X server that has XFixes (nearly all real ones do), or try window mode instead of overlay. Some bare VNC or test servers leave it out.

x11.c|the X server has no 32 bit visual,.what: The overlay needs a 32 bit TrueColor visual for transparency and the X server doesnt offer one. Comes from `goome_open`.
x11.c|the X server has no 32 bit visual,.fix: Run on a server with a 32 bit visual (any normal desktop has one), or use window mode without `GOOME_WINDOW_TRANSPARENT`. Some VNC servers with a 24 bit screen are the usual cause.

x11.c|the X server said no while making.what: An X protocol error came back while `goome_open` was creating the overlay window and buffers. `<n>` is the X error code, I dont know which request set it off.
x11.c|the X server said no while making.fix: Try again and check the terminal for an X error line. If it repeats, tell me the error number and your desktop and X server.

x11.c|the desktop wont give keyboard foc.what: `goome_keyboard` (keyboard capture) asked for focus, but on Wayland the desktop wouldnt give it to our XWayland window, and a grab there wouldnt see keys going to native apps anyway.
x11.c|the desktop wont give keyboard foc.fix: On a Wayland session run the app with the Wayland backend if you need keyboard input, or log into an X11 session. Clicking the overlay first can also help.

x11.c|couldnt grab the keyboard (X said.what: `goome_keyboard` tried an X keyboard grab and it failed, `<n>` is the X grab status. Most often another app already holds a grab, or a menu is open.
x11.c|couldnt grab the keyboard (X said.fix: Close whatever has the keyboard (menus, screen lockers, other grabbing tools) and call it again.

x11.c|couldnt grab the pointer (X said <.what: The pointer grab from `goome_grab` failed, `<n>` is the X status. Another app is holding the mouse, or the window wasnt visible yet.
x11.c|couldnt grab the pointer (X said <.fix: Let go of any open menu or drag in another app and call it again. Make sure the window is mapped before grabbing.

x11.c|the window manager wont give our w.what: `goome_grab` asked the window manager to focus our window and it didnt. The grab itself may still have worked.
x11.c|the window manager wont give our w.fix: Try again after the window is shown. Some window managers block focus stealing, so turn that off or click the window once.

x11.c|hotkey <id> is taken by another ap.what: `goome_hotkey` couldnt grab hotkey `<id>`. Either another app already owns that key combo, or the key has no keycode on the current keyboard layout.
x11.c|hotkey <id> is taken by another ap.fix: Pick a different key or modifier combo, or close the app that has it. Check the key actually exists in your layout, see [hotkeys](hotkeys.md).

x11.c|out of memory.what: A plain `calloc` failed while opening X11 window mode (`goome_open`) or capture (`goome_capture`).
x11.c|out of memory.fix: Real out of memory, theres nothing the app can do except free some and retry.

x11.c|the X server has no 24 bit visual.what: Window mode needs a 24 bit TrueColor visual when the window isnt transparent, and the X server doesnt have one. Comes from `goome_open`.
x11.c|the X server has no 24 bit visual.fix: Use a server with a 24 bit visual, or ask for `GOOME_WINDOW_TRANSPARENT` so it picks the 32 bit one. Very odd or 16 bit setups cause this.

x11.c|the X server said no while making.what: An X protocol error came back while `goome_open` was building the window in window mode. `<n>` is the X error code and I dont know which request caused it.
x11.c|the X server said no while making.fix: Try again and watch the terminal for the X error line. If it repeats, tell me the number, your desktop and X server.

x11.c|the window is gone.what: A window call (`goome_window_*` position lookup) or a window capture found the X window no longer exists, or couldnt be translated to screen coordinates.
x11.c|the window is gone.fix: The window was closed or destroyed, so reopen it with `goome_open` before using it again.

x11.c|no window manager running, nobody.what: `goome_window_*` state changes (minimize, maximize, fullscreen) need a window manager to carry them out, and none is running.
x11.c|no window manager running, nobody.fix: Start a window manager, or skip state changes on bare X servers. Size and position calls still work.

x11.c|no window manager running, nobody.what: `goome_window_*` drag asks the window manager to move or resize the window, and there isnt one running.
x11.c|no window manager running, nobody.fix: Run under a window manager, or move the window yourself with the position and size calls.

x11.c|no mouse button is down.what: `goome_window_*` drag was called when goome didnt see a mouse button held on the window, so theres nothing to drag with.
x11.c|no mouse button is down.fix: Only start the drag from inside a mouse down event handler, while the button is still held.

x11.c|the X server wont give us the clip.what: `goome_clipboard_set` tried to become the clipboard owner and the X server didnt hand it over.
x11.c|the X server wont give us the clip.fix: Try again. If it keeps failing, another clipboard tool may be fighting for ownership, so close clipboard managers to test.

x11.c|lost the X server.what: `goome_clipboard_get` was waiting on the clipboard and the X connection dropped.
x11.c|lost the X server.fix: The X server went away or the session ended. Reopen goome once the server is back.

x11.c|the app that owns the clipboard di.what: `goome_clipboard_get` asked the app owning the clipboard for its text and got no reply in about 250 ms, twice if the first format failed.
x11.c|the app that owns the clipboard di.fix: Try again, the other app may be busy or frozen. Copying something again from a different app usually clears it.

x11.c|DISPLAY isnt set, no X server to g.what: `goome_capture` on X11 found no `DISPLAY` variable, so theres no screen to grab from.
x11.c|DISPLAY isnt set, no X server to g.fix: Set `DISPLAY` or run from inside the desktop session. From ssh or a service its usually missing.

x11.c|the screen is <bpp> bits a pixel,.what: `goome_capture` got an image from X that isnt 24 or 32 bits per pixel, which goome cant convert.
x11.c|the screen is <bpp> bits a pixel,.fix: Switch the screen to 24 or 32 bit color depth. 16 bit and 8 bit displays arent supported.

x11.c|odd pixel layout, red mask <mask>.what: `goome_capture` got an image whose red channel mask `<mask>` isnt one goome knows how to convert, only common 8 bit layouts and 10 bit depth 30.
x11.c|odd pixel layout, red mask <mask>.fix: Try a standard 24 or 32 bit depth. If your normal desktop hits this, tell me the mask value.

x11.c|that rect is off the screen.what: `goome_capture` was asked for a rect that doesnt overlap the screen after clipping, so there is nothing to grab.
x11.c|that rect is off the screen.fix: Pass a rect that sits at least partly on the screen, and check its width and height are above zero.

x11.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> grab.what: `goome_capture` couldnt allocate the output buffer for a `<w>`x`<h>` grab.
x11.c|no memory for a <w>x<h> grab.fix: A real out of memory. Grab a smaller rect if you can, otherwise free some memory.

x11.c|XGetImage failed, the screen chang.what: `goome_capture` asked X for the pixels and the request failed or raised an X error, most likely the screen size changed mid grab or the area became invalid.
x11.c|XGetImage failed, the screen chang.fix: Just try the capture again. If it fails every time, tell me your resolution and setup.

x11.c|cant find libX11.so.6.what: goome loads libX11 at runtime and couldnt find it, so `goome_open` and `goome_capture` cant use X11.
x11.c|cant find libX11.so.6.fix: Install it, package `libx11-6` on Debian and Ubuntu, `libX11` on Fedora, `libx11` on Arch.

x11.c|cant find libXfixes.so.3.what: goome loads libXfixes at runtime and couldnt find it, so X11 can be used by neither `goome_open` nor `goome_capture`.
x11.c|cant find libXfixes.so.3.fix: Install it, package `libxfixes3` on Debian and Ubuntu, `libXfixes` on Fedora, `libxfixes` on Arch.

x11.c|libX11 has no <symbol>.what: The libX11 or libXfixes on this machine is missing the function `<symbol>` that goome looks up when loading, so X11 cant be used.
x11.c|libX11 has no <symbol>.fix: Update the X libraries (`libx11-6`, `libxfixes3`) to a normal current version. A stripped or very old build is the usual cause.
